claim_a: 'The present General Motors Corporation was incorporated under the laws of Delaware on October 13, 1916'
claim_b: a New Jersey 'General Motors Company' existed from 1908-09-16 and was succeeded; a fourth person of the same name (CIK 1467858) starts 2009-07-16
why_they_differ: one name covering four registrations; no dissolution by operation of law between 1916 and 2009
evidence_weight: the two held carriers agree; the 2009 person is proven by machine resolution of the name
best_supported_interpretation: the 1908 date belongs to the New Jersey Company and is NOT the founding of the Delaware Corporation nor of the 2009 registrant
residual_uncertainty: whether the 1916 securities exchange was continuation or fresh promotion

claim_a: 1908-09-16 is the date the company was 'organized'
claim_b: 1908-09-16 is the date Durant 'effected the incorporation'
why_they_differ: a corporate short note compresses promotion steps; a historian separates filing from organisation
evidence_weight: compatible in substance; they differ only in what the date denotes
best_supported_interpretation: record the date as incorporation with the registrant's own word beside it

claim_a: Durant effected the 1908 incorporation; David Buick the 1900 nucleus; the syndicate the 1910 refounding
claim_b: no person is named at either date by the registrant's own note, by the 1929 paper, or by the 1920 brochure
why_they_differ: narrative history assigns agency; corporate notes and advertisements do not
evidence_weight: the only person-bearing account held is one retrospective book
best_supported_interpretation: Durant and Buick are supportable; 'and others' is supportable only as separate acts on separate dates

claim_a: General Motors went into receivership in 1910
claim_b: the five receivership occurrences in FH28 attach to Electric Vehicle (1907), United States Motor (1912), Chrysler (as the only receivership product), Lincoln (receiver's sale 1922-02-04); for GM in 1910 the print is a $15000000 note issue plus a voting-trust control transfer
why_they_differ: a keyword search for 'receiver' near '1910' in one book mints a fact from another firm's failure
evidence_weight: decisive against the premise on held bytes
best_supported_interpretation: 1910 was a change of control by contract, not a court receivership
residual_uncertainty: an unmentioned New Jersey equity proceeding remains possible [COR-04]

claim_a: Durant was expelled from GM in 1916
claim_b: held print gives 1910-11 loss of control while printed as vice-president, 1915 restoration as president of the GM Company, and a resignation announced 1920-11-30; Durant calls it a sale, du Pont calls it a request for management, Storrow calls the 1915 move a taking
why_they_differ: three interested speakers plus one premise with no carrier
best_supported_interpretation: record two exits, a contractual displacement 1910-11 and a financed resignation 1920-11-30; label 1916 unattested here
residual_uncertainty: whether the 1920 resignation covered an ouster [COR-05]

claim_a: the Fisher body merger happened in 1920
claim_b: four separate printed acts: Fisher incorporated New York 1916-08-21; 60 per cent interest taken 1919; cost-plus-17.6-per-cent contract 1919; absorption in 1926 by a spring-1926 agreement
why_they_differ: 'the Fisher merger' used loosely for control, contract and absorption
best_supported_interpretation: four register rows, four carrier lines; no 1920 Fisher act is printed
residual_uncertainty: the exact 1926 closing date and fiscal alignment of 1919/1920 figures [COR-06]

claim_a: the 1926-28 acquisitions were Fiat of Canada, Anderson, Sheridan and a London branch
claim_b: Fiat occurs 0 times in FH28; every Anderson hit is Ford's original stockholder John W. Anderson; Sheridan is a GM division organised 1920 and liquidated 1921-22; London hits are bibliographic imprints plus 'the Explosives Trades, Ltd. (of London, England)'; the Canadian entities printed are McLaughlin Motor Car Co., Ltd. and Canadian Chevrolet
why_they_differ: premises are memory of other firms' GM stories; GM-adjacent foreign/Canadian print sits in 1908-10, 1919-20 and 1929
evidence_weight: three of four unsupported on held bytes; the fourth supported but mis-typed
best_supported_interpretation: record refuted / refuted / supported-with-correction / UNTRIED and open the Canadian and London registry route as a gap, not a null
residual_uncertainty: real GM Canadian and UK incorporations are likely documented in families never queried [COR-07; COR-09: these adjacency counts are line-wise floors, not censuses]

claim_b: the earliest held naming of the registrant is a 1920 divisional brochure, and its 1908 first person belongs to Orville Wright
why_they_differ: a date asserted and a naming attested are different claim types; a GM-copyrighted document can carry a non-GM 'we'
best_supported_interpretation: founding act at Medium and lineage-capped; naming wall at 1920; no 1908-10 first-person GM voice may be implied
residual_uncertainty: a 1908-10 printed naming could still be found

claim_a: the general-motors-annual-reports item is an in-window 1918 carrier (TIER1_CANDIDATE_TEXT)
claim_b: the fetched file is gm1937_djvu.txt and its own first pages print 'TWENTY-NINTH ANNUAL REPORT ... YEAR ENDED DECEMBER 31, 1937'
